description: Neofolk is a post-industrial music subculture that emerged in the United Kingdom during the early 1980s out of post-punk and industrial music. It uses acoustic instrumentation, primarily acoustic guitars, piano, and strings, to explore European traditionalism, paganism, and the historical trauma of the 20th century. Where conventional folk music tends to preserve national custom, neofolk instead uses the acoustic folk form to stage apocalyptic lament and a rejection of modern, rationalist society, drawing heavily on 19th-century Romanticism and early 20th-century anti-modernist philosophy.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Anti-modernism, cultural lament, ambiguity, traditionalism, historical trauma
